term: Mistake 2 – Misapplying row operations on determinants
desc: : While $R_i \to R_i + k R_j$ keeps the determinant invariant, multiplying a row directly ($R_i \to k R_i$) scales the determinant by $k$. Remember to balance it outside the determinant!
: Writing $|2A| = 2|A|$ instead of $2^n|A|$ is a guaranteed point-loss trap. Always verify the order $n$ first.

term: Mistake 4 – Forgetting to Transpose the Cofactor Matrix
desc: : The adjoint is the transpose of the cofactor matrix ($\operatorname{adj}(A)= C^{\top}$). Many students compute the cofactors but forget to transpose them.

term: Mistake 5 – Trying to take the determinant of a non-square matrix
desc: : Determinants are strictly defined only for square ($n \times n$) matrices.
: If a matrix can be converted to upper (or lower) triangular form using only row addition/subtraction, the determinant is simply the product of the diagonal entries.
: For a block diagonal matrix $\begin{bmatrix}P & 0\\0 & Q\end{bmatrix}$, the determinant is simply $\det(P)\cdot\det(Q)$. This reduces complex high-order problems instantly.
